details.description: Pale warm-grey concrete slabs form the shared central walking and riding surface.
Several broad transverse slab courses cross the central alley.
Green moss follows both long borders of the centre paving.
Branching thin cracks split the large slabs, especially the near and central panels.
A darker irregular exposed patch interrupts the near right portion of the central paving.
A dark elongated stain runs down the centre with scattered round oil spots nearby.
A broad irregular grey-brown stain marks the near left paving panel.
The far slabs contain separate rounded dark stains.
Lift-out rectangular concrete lids repeat down the left channel with transverse gaps.
The right channel has a distinct sequence of lids and larger black openings.
Missing lids expose very dark rectangular channel patches; these must read through material on the native quad.
The lids carry worn corners, damp dark patches and fine concrete grain.
Narrow outer strips border both channels; the explicit native contract keeps them flush.
Exactly 4 x 8 m at y=0, two triangles with a 3 m shared alley and .5 m band on each side; no raised kerb or separate sidewalk.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: One 4 x 8 m upward quad at y=0, two triangles and one draw/material/geometry; exact .5/3/.5 m bands.
Retain own central slab courses, branching cracks, moss margins, long oil stain, near damaged patch, distinct drain-lid sequences and dark openings.
No raised edge or recessed channel geometry. Depth, damp response and moss are material-only.
Compare original plate, rectangular flat diagnostic, four oblique views, controlled materials and repeated 0/180 alley joins.
Every review exceeds95 and installed/export evidence verifies the accepted source and maps.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

Material gate explicitly fails for the drain-lid region; failure is preserved and is not waived. The exact 4 x 8 m quad and .5/3/.5 m profile are correct. Both side channels are largely plain grey strips, missing the actual lid weathering and dark open sections. The original normal map creates extreme raised-looking slab edges and strong bright/dark changes between 0/180 neighbors under grazing light. Reconstruct own registered concrete, cracks, moss and asymmetric drain-lid/opening layout. Replace strongly biased original normals with independent fine grain and shallow explicit semantic relief. Review physical rectangular joins and retain the two-triangle native contract.
